title: Alongside
description: Alongside was a longitudinal treatment companion for cancer patients that used a persistent Jac graph to track daily check-ins, medications, and symptoms across fragmented care settings. Rather than top-k similarity retrieval, relevance was defined by graph reachability, enabling a mandatory traversal gate that blocked unsafe drug interactions before a new substance entered the regimen and surfaced unprompted concerns each time the app opened. The output was a citation-backed "Questions for your care team" page, turning a silent retrieval failure mode into an inspectable structural property with hard safety guarantees.

title: AI-Driven Resume Quality & ATS Analysis System
description: Built an end-to-end agentic resume tailoring system that ingests a user's resume, GitHub repositories, and LinkedIn data into a skills knowledge graph, then orchestrates a pipeline of LLM agents (via LangGraph and Anthropic/OpenAI models) to analyze a target job description, plan per-item edit actions, generate a constrained one-page resume, and score it algorithmically for ATS compatibility. The system exposed a React/TypeScript chat interface backed by a FastAPI server, enabling iterative revision cycles where proposed changes could be reviewed, approved, or rejected before being applied and exported to PDF or DOCX via LaTeX. Every tailoring run was logged to a PostgreSQL decision store with user satisfaction scores, creating a feedback loop to evaluate which tailoring strategies performed best over time.

title: Neetcode Submissions
description: Maintained a structured repository of algorithmic problem solutions in Python, automatically synced from NeetCode.io using GitHub integration. Solutions span core data structures and algorithms topics including arrays, binary search, dynamic programming, and graph traversal, organized by problem category and submission history. The repository serves as a versioned record of technical problem-solving progress across a curated set of coding interview preparation problems.

title: Portfolio
description: Built a personal portfolio website to showcase data science projects, experience, and resume using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript ES modules — no frameworks, bundlers, or build steps. Implemented a single-source-of-truth data layer in `data/site.js` that drives all four pages simultaneously, paired with Node.js scripts that automatically sync GitHub repository metadata and merge it back without overwriting editorial content. The result is a fully static, zero-dependency site deployable to any static host, with shared chrome, theming, and responsive layout handled through a lightweight custom component system.

title: RollAway
description: RollAway was a map-first progressive web app built exclusively for San Francisco mobile food vendors, ranking legal vending spots by scoring setback compliance, foot traffic, and competition using deterministic algorithms grounded in SF Public Works Order 182101, DataSF permit feeds, SFMTA closure data, and a full year of Bay Wheels trip history. The application encoded SF's four-agency permit process (Public Works, DPH, Fire Department, and Treasurer) into a single guided checklist, with LLMs used only to generate natural-language explanations from precomputed signals rather than for any legal or scoring logic. The stack combined a TypeScript/React PWA frontend with a Python backend, PostGIS spatial queries, and a PLpgSQL scoring pipeline to surface low-competition, legally compliant locations for a chosen time window.

title: AI Agent Policy Optimization
description: Built a reinforcement learning-based policy optimizer for an AI-driven HVAC contractor follow-up system, training an agent to select optimal outreach actions (such as estimate nudges, objection handling, escalation, or silence) across multi-turn homeowner conversations. Modeled the problem as a Markov Decision Process with a custom reward function balancing conversion rate, customer trust, opt-out risk, and escalation cost, then evaluated policies using simulated episode rollouts implemented in pure Python. The resulting policy outperformed a naive always-send baseline by reducing opt-outs and unnecessary touchpoints while maintaining comparable conversion on open estimates.

title: Diginetica: GNN vs. Flat Ranker for Session Recommendation
description: Built an end-to-end relational deep learning pipeline on the Diginetica (CIKM Cup 2016) e-commerce logs, using RelBench to convert the relational database into a heterogeneous graph — 8 node types (items, sessions, users plus view/query/click/queried-item/purchase events) and 22 edge types over 11 foreign-key relations. Engineered an `abs_time` event clock at microsecond resolution by folding intra-session millisecond offsets into the event date, enabling time-aware neighbor sampling that admits only neighbors strictly earlier than a per-row seed time so the receptive field never peeks at the future. Defined two tasks: session-conversion entity classification (binary, ~4% positive rate, AUPRC/AUROC) and next-item link prediction via intra-session leave-last-out on 218K sessions. The GNN is a two-tower heterogeneous GraphSAGE encoder (HeteroEncoder + temporal encoder) splitting into session and item towers scored by dot product, trained with sampled-softmax over in-batch and pool negatives. It is compared against an XGBoost LambdaRank ranker (`rank:ndcg`) over anchor-based 1-hop features — co-view, co-purchase, transition, category, popularity, price, is_repeat. A shared per-row candidate pool (co-view + transition + co-purchase + category + popularity backfill, built on train statistics only) lets both models rank the identical set, isolating ranking quality from candidate recall, with Optuna sweeps (persistent SQLite, median pruning) tuning both on Novel Recall@10. Evaluation decomposes Recall@10, NDCG@10, and MRR across slices — Repeat/Novel, popularity (Head/Torso/Tail), and session length — through a single masked `task.evaluate` code path, alongside structural ablations on hop depth, item-feature capacity, and scoring head (pooled dot vs. maxpool vs. ColBERT-style late interaction).

title: Idx_cont_training
description: Built an end-to-end MLOps pipeline for continuously training machine learning models on real estate listing data, implementing a streaming data architecture to retrain models as new listings became available. Leveraged LightGBM and XGBoost as core modeling frameworks alongside geospatial feature engineering with GeoPandas, and developed custom utility modules for outlier detection and missingness handling to maintain data quality throughout the pipeline. The system automated model retraining and versioning using scikit-learn and Joblib, enabling property price predictions to adapt dynamically to shifting market conditions.

title: Portfolio Live Editor
description: Built an Express.js proxy server that intercepted live HTTP responses from a personal portfolio site and injected a WYSIWYG editing overlay into every served page, enabling point-and-click content editing directly on the rendered site. The overlay communicated with a custom REST API to read and write changes to a source JSON data file in real time, bypassing any build pipeline or recompilation step. This replaced manual source file edits with an in-place visual interface, eliminating context-switching between the live site and raw data files during content iteration.

title: Real Time ML Feature Store And Quant Research Platform
description: Built a modular quantitative research platform combining a real-time ML feature store with an event-driven backtesting engine, supporting the full pipeline from data ingestion to model-gated trading signals. The system ingests daily OHLCV bars and corporate actions via Yahoo Finance, stores them in Parquet with a DuckDB query layer, and feeds engineered features into a Feast feature store consumed by a mean-reversion classifier used as a tax-loss harvesting gate. A wash-sale-aware rules engine, lot-level position tracker, and six sequentially dependent build phases were implemented in Python, with each component tested in isolation using pytest.

title: California Real Estate Price Prediction
description: Built a web application that predicts single-family residence prices across California using an ensemble of custom-trained machine learning models including XGBoost and LightGBM, deployed via a Streamlit interface with interactive Plotly visualizations. Engineered the pipeline with scikit-learn for preprocessing and feature engineering, incorporating real estate data to capture regional pricing patterns across California counties. The application enables users to input property characteristics and receive price predictions in real time, demonstrating end-to-end ML deployment from model training to a production-ready web interface.

title: eCommerce Session Review Analysis - Predicting Online Shopper Purchase Intent
description: Built classification models using Random Forest and XGBoost on 12,330 e-commerce browsing sessions to predict purchase intent, applying threshold tuning to maximize recall and reduce missed conversions, achieving approximately 90% accuracy. Applied K-Means clustering to segment shoppers into five behavioral archetypes, uncovering conversion rates ranging from 0.4% for bounce-prone visitors to 24.3% for high-intent consumers. Identified product browsing depth and administrative page engagement as the strongest purchase predictors using Python, scikit-learn, pandas, and seaborn.
